quote: In relative terms, StoneDB's bulk-insert throughput was about 54 percent higher than KVLite's.
problem: Table A2 gives 348 vs 212 thousand ops/s for bulk insert, which is about 64 percent higher (348/212 = 1.64), not 54.

quote: Under the mixed workload, KVLite's median p99 latency was 4.2 ms, the worst of the three, against 3.1 ms for StoneDB and 2.9 ms for Marlin.
problem: Table A3 gives KVLite p99 as 4.8 ms [4.5-5.2], not 4.2 ms. The figure is misquoted.

quote: Marlin's higher write throughput comes from its batched write-ahead log, which groups concurrent writes into a single append.
problem: Causal attribution is unsupported. A1 states no profiler, tracing or ablation runs were collected for any store; A7 only quotes a design-doc sentence.

quote: Marlin's write advantage holds regardless of storage hardware or durability settings.
problem: Overgeneralised. All results come from one machine and one batched-fsync setting (every 1,000 writes); A1 says per-write fsync was not tested.

quote: StoneDB sustains its mixed-workload throughput over long-running operation.
problem: A1 says the longest run was 6 minutes including warm-up and no soak or multi-hour run was performed, so long-running behaviour is not shown.

quote: Marlin's own documentation presents it as the right engine for write-intensive systems generally.
problem: A7 quotes the README as designed for write-intensive workloads whose reads mostly touch recently written keys. The body drops that qualifier.

quote: Marlin also serves random reads faster than StoneDB.
problem: A2 medians are 417 vs 402 with overlapping five-run ranges [391-426] and [395-410]. The body treats this gap as established, while calling the similar-sized 312 vs 301 gap unresolved.

quote: The appendix lists the software versions and configuration used, so that the run can be repeated.
problem: A1 says the in-house harness is not yet published and no external reproduction has been done, so the appendix alone does not allow the run to be repeated.

quote: Wray kept a continuous day-by-day record of the winter.
problem: E1 records a 46-day gap with no dated entries (12 Dec 1741 to 26 Jan 1742) and missing folios 31-34, so the record is not continuous.

quote: The parish register shows 52 burials in 1742, which is 23 more than in 1741.
problem: E5(a) gives 33 burials in 1741 and 52 in 1742, a difference of 19, not 23.

quote: Of the 29 death entries in the journal, Wray names a fever as the cause in seven.
problem: E5(b) says fever is named in 5 death entries, not 7.

quote: The frost alone accounts for the rise in burials in 1742.
problem: Unsupported causal claim. E5(b) names cold or frost in only 6 of 29 death entries and gives no cause for 18; the appendix contains no analysis of the rise.

quote: Wray's burial entries have been checked against the parish register and found accurate.
problem: Q8 says only nine burial notices were compared with the register and the remainder were not checked. The claim is generalised to all entries.

quote: Wray states that the vicar kept the tithe barn locked against the poor.
problem: Q5 (fol. 41r) is hearsay: 'It is said by some', and Wray says he has not seen it himself. Wray does not state it as fact.

quote: The journal gives a representative picture of how rural parishes in the county fared that winter.
problem: E1 says the edition covers one parish and prints no records or comparative material from any other parish, so representativeness cannot be established.

quote: Of the 48 nurses who were screened but not randomized, most (31) declined to take part.
problem: T2 shows the 48 non-randomized nurses were 31 ineligible and 17 who declined. The 31 were not decliners.

quote: Across both arms, 56 of 64 participants (85.9%) completed the week 8 assessment.
problem: 56 of 64 is 87.5%, as T2 states. The 85.9% figure is wrong.

quote: The reduction in insomnia severity persisted after the program ended.
problem: T1 says assessments were at baseline and week 8 only, with none after week 8, so persistence after the program cannot be shown.

quote: The sleep-restriction module is what drove the improvement.
problem: Protocol 3.1 says components are delivered together and the study does not test individual components. Attributing the effect to one module is unsupported.

quote: Engagement with the program was high.
problem: T5 shows a median of 5 of 8 modules, only 34.4% completed all eight, and 8 of 32 completed three or fewer. The appendix gives no basis for calling this high.

quote: These data show the program is safe for night-shift nurses.
problem: T6 reports two mild events from self-report in a 32-person arm, and Protocol 7.4 says the study is not powered to estimate adverse event rates. Safety cannot be shown.

quote: The findings apply to shift workers generally.
problem: T1 shows a single-centre, open-label pilot of 64 nurses from one teaching hospital. Generalisation to shift workers generally is unsupported.

quote: One of the four specimens reached the runout and the other three failed, the shortest at 1,138,000 cycles.
problem: F3 gives the 4.0 kN failure lives as 1,412,000, 1,865,000 and 1,238,000. The shortest is 1,238,000, not 1,138,000.

quote: At 4.0 kN the bracket has a 75 percent chance of failing before two million cycles.
problem: Only four specimens were tested at 4.0 kN, one flagged INTERRUPTED, and F2 says no statistical analysis was performed. Three of four is an observed fraction, not a failure probability.

quote: The mean life at 5.0 kN was about 483,000 cycles.
Below 3.0 kN the bracket has an effectively infinite fatigue life.
problem: No specimens were tested below 3.0 kN (F2, F3). This is extrapolation presented as a finding.

quote: The excess set in S08 is explained by its coming from a different material lot.
problem: The lab log says the lot B mill certificate is not on file and no sectioning, hardness or tensile tests on lot B are scheduled. The cause is untested; lot origin is only correlated with the result.

quote: The bracket's performance carries over to the full range of service temperatures.
problem: All tests were at 20.1-22.6 C with no tests at other temperatures (F2). REQ-EN-003 requires operation from -30 C to +50 C, so this is untested.

quote: The fatigue programme was run in accordance with ASTM E466.
problem: TP-221 says the method was 'adapted from' ASTM E466, with deviations listed in section 4 (four specimens per level against a plan of six, and load frame alignment not verified).
